text:
Situation: Insulin glulisine is listed by FDA as To Be Discontinued. Our three Corvale sites hold limited inventory: Corvale East 17 days (268 syringes), Corvale General 21 days (277.17 units), Corvale Lakeside 17 days (60 syringes). Other insulin products at each site have varying days on hand but are not the subject of this shortage.

Why (FDA record): FDA records show the Baxter Healthcare Corporation manufacturing plant received an OAI classification on 2026-04-02 and a Warning Letter on 2026-09-29. The Sanofi-Aventis Deutschland GmbH plant received an OAI classification on 2010-09-16 and a Warning Letter on 2011-02-08. Eli Lilly and Company's Indianapolis plant is not on FDA's shortage list for insulin glulisine as of 2026-10-21.

Our position: We must secure alternative supply immediately to avoid stockouts. The ranked sourcing options show five manufacturers not on FDA's shortage list today. Eli Lilly and Company is the top option by rule.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer initiates purchase agreement with Eli Lilly and Company for insulin glulisine; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
2. Buyer initiates purchase agreement with Novo Nordisk as secondary source; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
3. Buyer evaluates Biocon Biologics Inc., Civica, Inc., and Lanexa Biologics, LLC for tertiary supply; requires Pharmacy Director and P&T Committee approval for formulary addition.
4. Buyer allocates incoming stock proportionally across Corvale East, General, and Lakeside based on current days-on-hand; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
5. Buyer reports weekly inventory status to P&T Committee until all sites exceed 30 days supply; requires Pharmacy Director approval.

Not recommended: Delaying procurement pending further FDA action; relying solely on current Baxter or Sanofi labeled inventory; making clinical substitution decisions without treating clinician and committee review.
